intro.title: Typing Uncertain Output
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple TypeScript function that handles uncertain or optional data, like a user profile that might be missing some information. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's union types to explicitly declare when a value could be of multiple types, such as a string or undefined. The main constructs involved are type annotations and union types (using the | operator). This will help you write safer, more predictable code by telling TypeScript exactly what to expect from your functions.
intro.usecase: Typing uncertain output is essential for handling data from APIs, user inputs, or external libraries where values might be missing or unknown. In real-world applications, this pattern appears in dashboards that fetch live data (e.g., stock prices or sensor readings that could be null), forms with optional fields, or search filters that return partial results. By properly typing these uncertain outputs, developers can build more robust and predictable UIs, preventing runtime errors and improving user experience in products like e-commerce platforms, analytics tools, or content management systems.
